newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan doctors vote to continue strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan doctors vote to continue strike.

text.p: Venezuelan public doctors voted on Monday to continue an 11-day strike, plunging the country's shaky health system deeper into confusion.

Union representatives of the 25,000 doctors, who stopped work to demand a big pay increase, voted by a two-thirds majority to continue the strike that first hit the country's 380 hospitals on Dec. 27.
The vote, at an extraordinary meeting convened in Caracas, was 91 in favour and 45 against with no abstention.

The government had asked for a 48-hour truce, especially at emergency wards, to discuss its offer of a 25 percent wage increase. It is considering declaring a national health emergency that would entail a militarization of all hospitals.
"We've reached a dead end," Labour Minister Juan Nepomuceno Garrido told Reuters after the vote.
Doctors earn a minimum of $126 per month and an average of $304 monthly, including bonuses. They have demanded at least $735 a month.
Authorities say the strike has led to the deaths of up to 13 patients because of apparent lack of adequate medical care.
